'''Ettore Fiorini''' (19 April 1933 – 9 April 2023) was an Italian experimental particle physicist. He studied the physics of the [[weak interaction]] and was a pioneer in the field of [[double beta decay]]. He served as a professor of nuclear and subnuclear physics at the [[University of Milano-Bicocca]].<ref name="Università degli Studi di Milano-Bicocca 2017">{{cite web | title=FIORINI ETTORE | website=Università degli Studi di Milano-Bicocca | date=17 July 2017 | url=https://www.unimib.it/ettore-fiorini | language=it | access-date=22 September 2018 | archive-date=23 September 2018 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180923091322/https://www.unimib.it/ettore-fiorini | url-status=dead }}</ref>

== Early life ==
Fiorini was born on 19 April 1933 in [[Verona]]. His father was the eminent surgeon [[Enoch Fiorini]].<ref name="JINR">{{cite web| title=Ettore Fiorini| website=Dzhelepov Laboratory of Nuclear Problems| date=24 December 2014| url=http://dlnp.jinr.ru/en/45-premii/pontekorvo-prize/25-2014-12-24-11-30-48| access-date=22 September 2018}}</ref><ref name="Enoch">{{cite web| title=Enoch Fiorini| website=Accademia Roveretana degli Agiati| url=http://www.agiati.org/ara_abbonamenti.jsp?ID_LINK=113111&area=195&id_context=322533| language=it| access-date=22 September 2018}}{{Dead link|date=March 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref>

== Career ==
Fiorini graduated in physics from the [[University of Milan]] in 1955. After working as a research associate at [[Duke University]] from 1959 to 1969, he returned to Milan for the remainder of his academic career, except for a spell in Geneva at [[CERN]] (1979–82). He carried out the bulk of his research in Italy at the underground laboratories of [[Mont Blanc]] and [[Laboratori Nazionali del Gran Sasso|Gran Sasso]].<ref>{{cite web |title=FIORINI, Ettore in 'Enciclopedia Italiana' |website=www.treccani.it |url=http://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/ettore-fiorini_(Enciclopedia-Italiana) |language=it |access-date=23 September 2018}}</ref>

== Scientific achievements ==
Fiorini had a longstanding research interest in [[weak interaction]]s and related phenomena. In the 1970s he collaborated with [[André Lagarrigue]] to create the [[Gargamelle]] detector, a giant bubble chamber at [[CERN]], and with [[Carlo Rubbia]] and [[Riccardo Giacconi]] on [[neutrino]] experiments that contributed to the discovery of weak [[neutral currents]], thereby providing the first empirical test of the [[electroweak theory]].<ref name="JINR"/><ref name="Gargamelle">{{cite web | last1=Sapienza | first1=University of Rome La | last2=CERN. | first2=talked to Christine Sutton at | title=Neutral currents: A perfect experimental discovery – CERN Courier | website=CERN Courier – International Journal of High-Energy Physics | date=20 April 2014 | url=https://cerncourier.com/neutral-currents-a-perfect-experimental-discovery/ | access-date=22 September 2018}}</ref>

Fiorini was a pioneering investigator of [[neutrinoless double beta decay]]. In the 1960s he proposed and performed the first study of [[neutrinoless double beta decay]] (0νββ) in <sup>76</sup>Ge using [[germanium]] [[diode]]s.<ref name="diode">{{cite journal| last1=Fiorini| first1=E.| last2=Pullia| first2=A.| last3=Bertolini| first3=G.| last4=Cappellani| first4=F.| last5=Restelli| first5=G.| title=A search for lepton non-conservation in double beta decay with a germanium detector| journal=Physics Letters B| publisher=Elsevier BV| volume=25| issue=10| year=1967| issn=0370-2693| doi=10.1016/0370-2693(67)90127-x| pages=602–603| bibcode=1967PhLB...25..602F}}</ref> In subsequent decades he was involved with two far larger collaborations at underground facility of the [[Laboratori Nazionali del Gran Sasso]]: the [[Cuoricino|CUORICINO]]<ref>{{Cite journal |title=<sup>130</sup>Te neutrinoless double-beta decay with CUORICINO |journal=[[Astroparticle Physics]] |year=2011 |pages=822–831 |volume=34 |issue=11 |doi=10.1016/j.astropartphys.2011.02.002 |first=E. |last=Andriotti |collaboration=CUORICINO Collaboration |bibcode=2011APh....34..822A |arxiv=1012.3266 |s2cid=119185418 }}</ref> and [[CUORE]]<ref name="Arnaboldi Artusa Avignone Balata p. ">{{cite journal | last1=Arnaboldi | first1=C. | last2=Artusa | first2=D. R. | last3=Avignone | first3=F. The results of these experiments have relevance for the study of [[dark matter]] and solar [[axion]]s.<ref name="JINR"/>

In the 1980s he directed the [[NUSEX]] (Nucleon Stability Experiment) investigation of proton decay located in the Mont Blanc underground laboratory. NUSEX helped determine the limits of proton stability, applying innovative methods to correct for the background effects of cosmic rays.<ref name="JINR"/>

Fiorini also collaborated on the [[GALLEX]] project at Gran Sasso that provided the first observations of low-energy neutrinos produced by the initial proton fusion step of the [[proton-proton chain reaction]], confirming that this was the dominant fusion process occurring in the sun.<ref name="JINR"/><ref name="Gallex">{{cite web| title=Earlier Neutrino Physics Projects at MPIK| website=Max-Planck-Institut für Kernphysik| url=https://www.mpi-hd.mpg.de/lin/research_history.de.html| language=de| access-date=22 September 2018}}</ref>

His other research activities include the development of [[microbolometer]]s for X-ray [[spectroscopy]] and high-precision measurements of the transition energies and lifetimes of nuclei, results which could help measure the mass of [[antineutrino]]s.<ref name="JINR"/>

Fiorini later conducted several [[archaeometry|archaeometric]] studies, using non-destructive techniques such as [[neutron activation analysis]] to discover the properties of historical materials. He proved, using samples of [[Napoleon]]'s hair, that the former emperor did not die from arsenic poisoning.<ref name="Napoleon">{{cite news| last=Highfield| first=Roger| title=Napoleon didn't die from arsenic poisoning| work=[[The Daily Telegraph]]| date=11 February 2008| url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/science/science-news/3324879/Napoleon-didnt-die-from-arsenic-poisoning.html| access-date=23 September 2018}}</ref> Another project demonstrated the provenance of lead ingots from a Roman shipwreck &mdash; before repurposing them for the lining of the CUORE detector.<ref name="Nosengo">{{cite journal| last=Nosengo| first=Nicola| title=Roman ingots to shield particle detector| journal=Nature| publisher=Springer Nature| date=15 April 2010| issn=1476-4687| doi=10.1038/news.2010.186| doi-access=free}}</ref><ref name="The Cyprus Institute">{{cite web| title=Prof. Ettore Fiorini Delivers Second Enrico Fermi Lecture on Archaeometallurgy| website=The Cyprus Institute| date=5 May 2017| url=https://www.cyi.ac.cy/index.php/in-focus/prof-ettore-fiorini-delivers-second-enrico-fermi-lecture-on-archaeometallurgy.html| access-date=23 September 2018}}</ref><ref name="Cossi">{{cite web| author=cossi| title=NOBEL INGOTS| website=Istituto Nazionale di Fisica Nucleare| date=16 June 2015| url=http://home.infn.it/en/progetti-foe/ital-rad/114-press-release/press-release-2016/1759-nobel-ingots| access-date=23 September 2018| archive-date=23 September 2018| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180923085511/http://home.infn.it/en/progetti-foe/ital-rad/114-press-release/press-release-2016/1759-nobel-ingots| url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Death ==
Fiorini died on 9 April 2023, at the age of 89.<ref>[https://www.meteoweb.eu/2023/04/morto-ettore-fiorini-maestro-studi-neutrini/1001226092/ E' morto Ettore Fiorini, maestro degli studi sui neutrini] {{in lang|it}}</ref>

== Awards ==
Fiorini received the 2007 [[Enrico Fermi Prize]] in recognition for his work on weak neutral currents and solar neutrinos.<ref name=EnricoFermiItaly>{{cite news| title=Italian Physical Society "Enrico Fermi" Prize| url=http://en.sif.it/activities/fermi_award| publisher=Italian Physical Society| quote=for his contribution to the discovery of weak neutral currents and to the study of solar neutrinos.}}</ref> For his work on neutrinoless double beta decay, he was awarded the 2012 [[Bruno Pontecorvo Prize]].<ref>{{cite web| url=http://dubna-oez.ru/news/362.htm| title=Историческое место Европейского физического общества открыто в Дубне| language=ru| trans-title=The historical site of the European Physical Society was opened in Dubna| date=25 February 2013| access-date=21 September 2018| quote=за выдающийся вклад в поиск безнейтринного двойного бета-распада ({{Translation|for his outstanding contribution to the search for neutrinoless double beta decay}})| archive-date=22 September 2018| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180922024734/http://dubna-oez.ru/news/362.htm}}</ref> He has been a corresponding member of the {{lang|it|[[Accademia Nazionale dei Lincei]]}} since 1988.
